questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Introduces a practical blue/green ECS deployment pattern with CodeDeploy, a common beginner-friendly scenario that touches IaC, traffic shifting, health checks, and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- ECS blue/green via CodeDeploy for ECS
- Minimal CloudFormation for deployment controller and target groups
- Canary traffic shifting and health-check gating
- Rollback criteria via CloudWatch alarms and deployment config
- IAM least-privilege roles scoped to needed services

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  MyECSService:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    Properties:
      DeploymentController:
        Type: CODE_DEPLOY
      LoadBalancers:
        - TargetGroupArn: !Ref BlueTargetGroup
          ContainerName: my-app
          ContainerPort: 80

  BlueTargetGroup:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
    Properties:
      HealthCheckPath: /health
      HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 30
      HealthCheckTimeoutSeconds: 5
      HealthyThresholdCount: 2

  GreenTargetGroup:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
    Properties:
      HealthCheckPath: /health
      HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 30
      HealthCheckTimeoutSeconds: 5
      HealthyThresholdCount: 2

  DeploymentGroup:
    Type: AWS::CodeDeploy::DeploymentGroup
    Properties:
      ApplicationName: !Ref ECSApplication
      DeploymentConfigName: CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent5Minutes
      ServiceRoleArn: !Ref CodeDeployRole
      DeploymentStyle:
        DeploymentType: BLUE_GREEN
        DeploymentOption: WITH_TRAFFIC_CONTROL
      BlueGreenDeploymentConfiguration:
        TerminateBlueInstancesOnDeploymentSuccess: true
        DeploymentReadyOption:
          ActionOnTimeout: CONTINUE_DEPLOYMENT
        GreenFleetProvisioningOption:
          Action: DISCOVER_EXISTING
      AlarmConfiguration:
        Alarms:
          - Name: !Ref HealthCheckAlarm
          - Name: !Ref ErrorRateAlarm
        AlarmAction: ROLLBACK_DEPLOYMENT

  HealthCheckAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      MetricName: HealthyHostCount
      Namespace: AWS/ApplicationELB
      Statistic: Minimum
      Threshold: 1
      ComparisonOperator: LessThanThreshold
      EvaluationPeriods: 2

  ErrorRateAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      MetricName: HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count
      Namespace: AWS/ApplicationELB
      Statistic: Sum
      Threshold: 10
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
      EvaluationPeriods: 2
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design risk-controlled feature flags in a serverless setup, plus automated testing and rollback integration.

## Key Concepts
- AWS AppConfig for feature flags
- CodePipeline and CodeBuild integration
- CloudFormation IaC for infrastructure
- Rollout percentages and automatic rollback

## Code Example
```yaml
# CloudFormation snippet (partial)
Resources:
  AppConfigApplication:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Application
    Properties:
      Name: ServerlessApiApp

  AppConfigEnvironment:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Environment
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref AppConfigApplication
      Name: Production

  AppConfigConfigurationProfile:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::ConfigurationProfile
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref AppConfigApplication
      Name: FeatureFlags
      LocationUri: hosted

  AppConfigHostedConfigurationVersion:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::HostedConfigurationVersion
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref AppConfigApplication
      ConfigurationProfileId: !Ref AppConfigConfigurationProfile
      Content: '{"search-v2-enabled": {"value": false, "enabled": true, "type": "Boolean"}}'
      ContentType: application/json

  AppConfigDeployment:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Deployment
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref AppConfigApplication
      ConfigurationProfileId: !Ref AppConfigConfigurationProfile
      ConfigurationVersion: !Ref AppConfigHostedConfigurationVersion
      Environment: !Ref AppConfigEnvironment
      DeploymentStrategy: Rolling_10PercentEvery10Minutes
```

## Testing Steps
1. Deploy CloudFormation stack to create AppConfig resources
2. Update Lambda function to read the feature flag from AppConfig
3. Configure CodeBuild stage in CodePipeline to:
   - Query AppConfig for flag status
   - Run smoke tests against /search-v2 when flag is enabled
   - Fail the build if tests fail (triggers pipeline rollback)
4. Set initial rollout to 10% in AppConfig deployment strategy
5. Monitor metrics and gradually increase rollout percentage
6. On complete rollout, update flag to 100% or remove the flag entirely

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design scalable, isolation-focused pipelines across AWS accounts, with per-tenant config, controlled traffic shifts, and automated rollback. It also checks cross-account IAM, IaC discipline, and integration of synthetic monitoring into deployments.

## Code Example

```yaml
# Example GitHub Actions workflow snippet
name: tenant-deploy
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        tenant: [prod, acct-101, acct-202]
    steps:
      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v1
        with:
          role-duration-seconds: 3600
      - name: Deploy tenant via CDK/CFN
        run: |
          npm install
          npm run cdk:deploy -- --tenant ${{ matrix.tenant }}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design controlled, policy-driven DR chaos experiments across regions with proper guardrails and observability.

## Key Concepts

- **Cross-region DR with chaos engineering**: Using AWS FIS to inject controlled failures and validate failover mechanisms
- **Traffic management**: Istio traffic shifting and Route 53 latency-based routing for seamless failover
- **Data consistency**: MSK replication controls and validation of data integrity across regions
- **Policy enforcement**: OPA Gatekeeper for experiment guardrails and IAM Roles Anywhere for secure workload access
- **GitOps-driven automation**: FluxCD overlays for DR state management and reproducible runbooks

## Code Example

```yaml
# FIS experiment manifest skeleton
apiVersion: aws FIS/v1
kind: Experiment
metadata:
  name: dr-chaos-test
  region: us-east-1
spec:
  description: "Cross-region DR chaos experiment"
  tags:
    approved: "true"
    environment: "dr-test"
  targets:
    msk-replication:
      resourceType: "aws:msk:cluster"
      selector:
        clusterArn: "arn:aws:msk:us-east-1:123456789012:cluster/shared-cluster"
    eks-workloads:
      resourceType: "aws:eks:pod"
      selector:
        clusterName: "eks-primary"
  actions:
    pause-replication:
      actionId: "aws:msk:pause-replication"
      parameters:
        duration: "60s"
    steer-traffic:
      actionId: "aws:eks:interrupt-pod"
      parameters:
        mode: "random"
        percentage: "50"
```

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  EastHealthCheck:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HealthCheck
    Properties:
      HealthCheckConfig:
        Type: HTTP
        FullyQualifiedDomainName: api-east.example.com
        Port: 80
        ResourcePath: /
        Interval: 30
        FailureThreshold: 3
  EastRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      Name: api.example.com
      Type: A
      SetIdentifier: East
      Failover: PRIMARY
      TTL: 60
      HealthCheckId: !Ref EastHealthCheck
  WestHealthCheck:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HealthCheck
    Properties:

        Type: HTTP
        FullyQualifiedDomainName: api-west.example.com
        Port: 80
        ResourcePath: /
        Interval: 30
        FailureThreshold: 3
  WestRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      Name: api.example.com
      Type: A
      SetIdentifier: West
      Failover: SECONDARY
      TTL: 60
